meta.title: The Kids Who Hacked the World, Part 3: The 15-Year-Old Who Hacked the CIA Director
meta.working_title: The 15-Year-Old Who Hacked the Head of the CIA (The Kids Who Hacked the World, Part 3)
meta.device: A 'TARGETS' board of government job titles (no faces) that get a red X one by one, and a phone that keeps ringing on a desk in a dark US government office while a teenager's bedroom glows across the ocean.
meta.style: Internet-crime caper in the house 2D style, Gumball/t-shirt character style (same as Parts 1-2). Painted plates: a small bedroom on an English housing estate, a US teenager's room with a satellite dish on the roof, a dark Washington office, a WikiLeaks-style document page, an FBI raid, a UK courtroom. Officials (CIA director, intelligence chief, FBI deputy) shown only as job-title cards and silhouettes, never likeness; Snowden shown only as a newspaper headline. Members identified by their online handles only (one was a minor). Methods described only as 'tricking customer support' and 'password resets'; no how-to. SFX under the VO (phone rings, typing, door ram, gavel), music at combine.
meta.source: English compilation transcript 'The Kids Who Hacked the World', segment 2 (~3,700 words), drawing on Darknet Diaries and press coverage. Public court facts only. Animal-cruelty segment, profanity, prank-call audio and the closing politics segment cut. Fully rewritten.

shots.vo: October 2015. The head of the CIA gets a call on his private phone from a number he doesn't know. The caller laughs at him, and says he's already inside his email.
shots.visual: A dark Washington office; a phone ringing on a desk; a silhouette in a chair. Job card: 'DIRECTOR, CIA'.

shots.vo: On the other end: a 15-year-old in his bedroom on a housing estate in England. He calls himself Cracka.
shots.visual: A small English bedroom; a teen with a phone, a laptop glowing.
shots.anim: He hangs up; stares at the phone.

shots.vo: His crew, Crackas With Attitude, would embarrass the US intelligence world for months, and land its members in prison.
shots.visual: A TARGETS board of job titles; red Xs appearing.
Title over the board.
shots.onscreen: THE KIDS WHO HACKED THE WORLD · PART 3

shots.vo: 2008, Virginia. An American teenager who goes by 'Default' likes soccer, video games and his dog. His father works for the government.
shots.visual: A suburban house; a teen kicking a ball with a dog chasing it.

shots.vo: It starts with cheating in video games. Then he wants to know how computers really work, and how to make them do things they shouldn't.
shots.visual: A game screen with a cheat menu; then lines of code scrolling.

shots.vo: Online, the hacker collective Anonymous is everywhere, in the news, in chat rooms. He hangs around their channels and starts breaking into websites just to see if he can.
shots.visual: News headlines with a faceless mask logo; a chat window.

shots.vo: He gets paranoid about being caught. He connects through a satellite dish to a free Wi-Fi network half a mile away, and keeps every device encrypted.
shots.visual: A satellite dish on a roof pointing at a distant fast-food sign.

shots.vo: He also buys Bitcoin early. By his own account, more than a thousand coins, kept on a hard drive in his room.
shots.visual: A hard drive glowing on a shelf; Bitcoin coins stacked beside it.

shots.vo: In 2013, a US intelligence contractor called Edward Snowden leaks secret documents showing how much the US government could see of people's communications.
shots.visual: A newspaper front page: 'NSA SURVEILLANCE LEAK'.

shots.vo: Months earlier, America's intelligence chief had told Congress the government did not collect data on millions of Americans. The leaks suggested otherwise. He later said he gave the 'least untruthful' answer he could.
shots.visual: A congressional hearing; a job card 'DIRECTOR OF NATIONAL INTELLIGENCE' at the witness table.
shots.anim: Gavel taps; quote card slides in.

shots.vo: For Default, that's personal. He wants the people who run surveillance to know how it feels to be watched.
shots.visual: Default's room; the TARGETS board taking shape on his wall.

shots.vo: In England, 15-year-old Cracka is angry too, especially about US foreign policy in the Middle East. In 2015 he starts Crackas With Attitude.
shots.visual: A housing estate; Cracka's window lit; a crew logo appears.

shots.vo: Top of their list: the director of the CIA. Cracka finds his phone company, then calls its support line pretending to be one of its own technicians.
shots.visual: Cracka on the phone; a call-centre worker at a headset on the other side.

shots.vo: The support worker believes him and reads out private account details. With enough personal details, Cracka persuades the email company to reset the password.
shots.visual: A padlock on an email icon clicking open.

shots.vo: He's now inside the CIA director's personal email account. Then come the prank calls to his phone, and to his family.
shots.visual: The ringing phone on the dark desk, over and over.

shots.vo: Nobody knows who's behind it, or what they want. The director's security has to treat it as a real threat.
shots.visual: Security agents closing blinds; a family car leaving in a hurry.

shots.vo: In the inbox are old work documents, including his security-clearance application: a long form full of private personal details.
shots.visual: A thick form with a 'CLEARANCE APPLICATION' header, sections redacted.

shots.vo: Cracka posts screenshots, then sends documents to WikiLeaks, which publishes them in October 2015.
shots.visual: A document page on a leak website; a big PUBLISHED stamp.

shots.vo: Asked on TV how hard the hack was, out of ten, Cracka answers: one.
shots.visual: A TV interview graphic; a big '1/10'.

shots.vo: They don't stop. They break into accounts of America's intelligence chief, and of the FBI's deputy director.
shots.visual: The TARGETS board: two more red Xs.

shots.vo: They get into a Justice Department system and leak names and contact details of thousands of US government employees.
shots.visual: A long staff list scrolling past, names blurred.

shots.vo: Default later said that by then, all bets were off. He wanted chaos to make people pay attention.
shots.visual: Default in a dark room, screens everywhere, a cracked mirror effect.

shots.vo: Default is careful for years. Then, one night, drunk on an Xbox voice chat, he brags to a friend: that CIA hack on the news? That was us.
shots.visual: Default with a headset, a speech bubble 'THAT WAS US'.
shots.anim: Bubble pops; friend's icon goes quiet.

shots.vo: He believes that friend turned him in. Armed FBI agents raid his room just as his computer finishes unlocking, and copy the drive before it locks again.
shots.visual: Agents bursting through a door; a laptop screen showing 'UNLOCKED'.

shots.vo: They take the hard drive with his Bitcoin on it.
shots.visual: An evidence bag sealing over a hard drive.

shots.vo: In England, police raid Cracka too. More arrests follow in the US and the UK.
shots.visual: A UK police van outside a housing estate at dawn.

shots.vo: Because he was a minor in the UK, Cracka got two years in youth detention. He has since kept his head down.
shots.visual: A gavel; a 2 YEARS card.

shots.vo: Default, an adult in the US, got five years in federal prison. In court he said he'd thought he was doing the right thing, and later realised he was completely wrong.
shots.visual: A US federal court; a 5 YEARS card; a quote card.

shots.vo: The scary part: the most powerful spy in the world was hacked by a teenager with a phone and a convincing voice. Protect your accounts with more than personal details.
shots.visual: The ringing phone on the desk goes quiet; a padlock with two keys appears.

shots.vo: Next: the teenager who grew up to become the most wanted hacker in America, and talked his way into almost anything.
shots.visual: A 1980s payphone with a WANTED poster beside it.
End card.
shots.onscreen: THE KIDS WHO HACKED THE WORLD · PART 4 NEXT

hooks: A 15-year-old in England called the head of the CIA on his private phone, and told him he was already in his email.
Asked how hard it was to hack the CIA director, out of ten, he said: one.

fixes: Brennan's AOL account hacked October 2015; WikiLeaks published documents 21 Oct 2015 including his SF-86.
Cracka (named in UK reporting as a minor at the time) sentenced April 2018 to 2 years youth detention; referred to by handle only.
D3F4ULT sentenced 2017 to 5 years federal prison; handle only.
Clapper's March 2013 Senate answer and later 'least untruthful' comment: worded neutrally.
'Thousands of employees' used for the FBI/DHS staff lists (Feb 2016), as counts vary (source said 9,000 DOJ).
1,000 BTC claim attributed to Default ('by his own account').
Student-debt deletion claim and Denmark animal-rights campaign cut (unverifiable / not suitable).
